name: Addon review tool
description:
## Why?

Reviewers have no single place showing the state of partner addon pull requests. Review tasks and capacity live in Jira, but the review state itself is spread across individual PRs — reviewers keep them open in browser tabs with ad-hoc naming to remember which ones wait on the partner. There is no way to see at a glance which PR waits on us, which waits on the partner, and how long it has been idle. Product needs that throughput picture to plan how many addons we can process.

## What?

**1. Overview of open pull requests**

GitHub is the spine: walk repositories with the Addon Repository GitHub App installed and take all open PRs. This does not depend on how consistently Jira is filled in.

Per PR, show:

- review state
- whether a response is already on the PR
- **whether it waits on us or on the partner**
- time since the last response

"Waits on whom" is read from the **review request** on the PR: a review requested from us means it waits on us, no open request means it waits on the partner. This is a GitHub mechanic we do not maintain by hand — submitting a review consumes the request, and the partner re-requesting a review after fixes flips the PR back to us.

Requesting a review is therefore **required from PR authors** — on opening the PR and after every round of fixes. That requirement is the price of a flow with no hand-maintained state and no guessing.

**2. Running the review and approving comments**

- The reviewer starts the review with a **button** on a given PR. Findings appear as pending in the interface. The button also re-runs the review. There is no automatic trigger on PR open in this round.
- On a **re-run** the skill loads its own previous comments from the PR itself and compares them against the code changes since the reviewed commit, so each finding comes back classified as new / still open / fixed. The reviewer does not re-triage what the partner has already fixed.
- Findings are **not sent automatically**. The reviewer goes through them, discards the ones that are wrong, and sends the rest.
- Comments are posted under the `shoptet-addon-reviewer` identity, following our standards — with icons, in English.
- **All comments are handled here. Merge stays in the PR.**

Going through and discarding findings in the interface is not only ergonomics — it is the only place where we can see the **share of discarded findings**, i.e. whether the skill is working or missing the mark.

A round of human code review still follows the AI round.

**3. The review engine is the skill, not a reimplementation**

The review is performed by the `st-addon-review` skill from the `shoptet-addon-review` plugin — Roman's implementation in [https://github.com/shoptet/addon-repository-actions-config/pull/7](https://github.com/shoptet/addon-repository-actions-config/pull/7). The tool invokes that skill; it does not carry its own copy of the rules. Rule changes then happen in one place and re-runs behave the same however the review was started.

The skill is **moved** out of `addon-repository-actions-config` into the AI review tool's repository — one home, not two diverging ones. It stays **internal for now**; whether it is published, and where, is decided separately once the tool is in use.

## Nice-to-have

- **Ask** — a chat in the interface where the reviewer can ask about the code and about the prepared comments before deciding what to send.
- **Regenerate a comment** — re-generate a single finding with a note ("too harsh", "say it in one sentence", "point at the right line") when the reviewer agrees with the finding but not the wording.

## Acceptance Criteria

The whole chain verified on one real pull request:

- ☐ The interface runs on the infrastructure and the team can reach it
- ☐ The overview lists open PRs from repositories with the Addon Repository GitHub App installed
- ☐ For each PR the overview shows review state, whether it waits on us or on the partner, and time since the last response
- ☐ "Waits on whom" is read from the review request on the PR; a partner re-requesting a review moves the PR back to "waits on us"
- ☐ A button starts the review on a given PR and produces pending findings; pressing it again re-runs the review
- ☐ A re-run classifies findings as new / still open / fixed from the skill's own previous comments and the code changes since the reviewed commit
- ☐ The review is executed by the `st-addon-review` skill, which lives in the tool's repository — the tool holds no second copy of the review rules
- ☐ The reviewer can discard individual findings and send the rest
- ☐ Sent comments appear on the pull request under `shoptet-addon-reviewer`
- ☐ Nothing is sent without the reviewer's action

## Deliberately not covered

- **"First round automatically."** The reviewer starts the review, so the first round still waits on human capacity. The agreement about an automatic first round is not fulfilled by this task and needs to be settled separately.
- **A partner reply without a re-requested review.** If a partner disputes a finding in a comment and does not re-request a review, the PR keeps showing as waiting on them. The overview shows idle time, which is where such a PR surfaces; enforcing the requirement on authors is a process matter, not a feature here.
- **Two-day response time.** The interface shows idle time; it does not enforce the SLA.
- **Capacity planning.** The interface gives throughput and age, not capacity — that stays in Jira.
- **Partner communication.** Partners will start receiving comments they did not get from a human, without being told in advance. Mitigated by the fact that a reviewer reads every comment before it is sent.
- **Publishing the skill.** It stays internal for this round.
